# Blender world authoring

> **Status:** `assets/world/world.blend` and `world.meta.json` are the source of
> truth. Runtime assets are committed outputs of `npm run world:export`; normal
> builds validate them without launching Blender.

## Source and generated files

The pipeline has one editable scene and one reviewable metadata sidecar:

```text
assets/world/world.blend       canonical spatial source
assets/world/world.meta.json   non-spatial gameplay metadata
```

It produces committed runtime files:

```text
public/models/world/level-visual.<hash>.glb.gz
public/models/world/level-collision.<hash>.glb.gz
public/models/world/level.json
```

Normal `npm run dev` and `npm run build` consume the committed runtime files
without requiring Blender. World authors run `npm run world:export` explicitly
and commit the `.blend`, sidecar, manifest, and both hashed assets together.

The authoring tools target **Blender 5.2 LTS**. Scene units are metres. Blender
is Z-up; glTF/Three.js is Y-up. Tools, rather than artists, own the conversion.

### Repository storage policy

The approximately 26 MiB `.blend` and 11 MiB compressed runtime asset set are
kept in ordinary Git for self-contained clones and simple CI/deploys. Do not add
Git LFS until binary history becomes a demonstrated repository-size problem; if
any single source/output approaches GitHub's 100 MiB limit, migrate all world
binaries to LFS in one dedicated change. Content-hashed outputs are replaced, not
retained side-by-side, in the working tree.

## Scene collections

`world.blend` uses this fixed hierarchy:

```text
WORLD
├── VISUAL
├── COLLISION
├── MARKERS
│   ├── SPAWNS
│   └── LIGHTS
└── METADATA
    ├── BUILDINGS
    ├── VOLUMES
    └── BOUNDS
```

Collection membership controls export. Prefixes make the Outliner readable but
are not authoritative; exporters read `cod_role` and the collection contract.
Every authored object has a stable `cod_id`. IDs are lowercase ASCII snake case
and must never be silently reused for a different object.

## Visual geometry

Visual meshes live under `WORLD/VISUAL` and carry:

| custom property | type | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `cod_role` | string | `visual` |
| `cod_id` | string | stable object identifier |
| `palette` | string | key in `src/world/palette.js` |
| `castShadow` | boolean | optional; defaults to true |
| `receiveShadow` | boolean | optional; defaults to true |
| `owLodDist` | number | optional positive LOD distance in metres |

During the migration, use one palette material per mesh. The Blender material
name should equal the `palette` key. Runtime materials remain generated by the
material subsystem; Blender materials are only viewport approximations.

Repeated objects must use linked mesh data. Blender's built-in glTF exporter does
**not** collapse ordinary linked duplicates even when `export_gpu_instances` is
enabled (that option currently targets Geometry Nodes instances). The world export
postprocessor therefore groups linked objects by `cod_instance_group` and emits
`EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing`. Applying transforms in a way that makes every copy unique
is a performance regression.

The one-time migration import stored original per-instance masks in the tool-owned
`cod_instance_color` property because Blender otherwise drops the extension's
`_COLOR_0` accessor while expanding instances. Do not edit `cod_instance_group`,
`cod_instance_index`, or `cod_instance_color` by hand.

Vertex colours are the existing `[wear, grime, ao]` masks and must survive the
round trip. UVs, normals, vertex colours, and instance transforms are required.

## Collision

Low-poly collision meshes live under `WORLD/COLLISION`. They are never included
in the visual GLB.

| custom property | type | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `cod_role` | string | `collision` |
| `cod_id` | string | stable collider identifier |
| `surface` | string | physics surface name |
| `cod_mask` | string | currently `world` |

Human-readable names use `COL_<surface>_<description>`, for example
`COL_concrete_w2_walls`. One object has one surface. Valid surface names are:

```text
concrete metal wood dirt sand glass water foliage fabric flesh rubber plaster
```

Collision meshes must have applied, finite transforms; no negative scale; and
triangle geometry after export. Prefer closed, low-poly proxies, but preserve
real openings such as doors and stairwells. Collision normals/UVs/vertex colours
are stripped from the runtime asset.

## Spawn markers

A spawn is an Empty in `WORLD/MARKERS/SPAWNS`:

| custom property | type | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `cod_role` | string | `spawn` |
| `cod_id` | string | stable spawn identifier |
| `cod_tag` | string | UI/debug label |
| `cod_team` | string | optional; defaults to `any` |

Blender local **+Y is gameplay forward**. The exporter converts that axis to a
world-space forward vector; runtime derives yaw from the vector. Do not copy a
Blender Euler component directly into the manifest.

Use an `ARROWS` Empty so the green local Y axis is visible. A spawn must be
inside playable bounds and have valid collision ground below it.

## Lights

Use real Blender Point lights under `WORLD/MARKERS/LIGHTS` for useful viewport
preview. Runtime behaviour is described by custom properties:

| custom property | type | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `cod_role` | string | `light` |
| `cod_id` | string | stable identifier |
| `cod_kind` | string | `interior` or `street` |
| `cod_range` | number | culling/radiance range in metres |
| `cod_priority` | integer | renderer light priority |
| `cod_day` | number | daytime intensity |
| `cod_night` | number | nighttime intensity |

Position and colour come from the Blender light. Runtime still drives intensity
from solar altitude and keeps point-light shader permutations stable.

## Buildings, volumes, and bounds

Building footprints are Cube empties under `WORLD/METADATA/BUILDINGS`:

| custom property | type | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `cod_role` | string | `building` |
| `cod_id` | string | stable building ID, e.g. `W2` |
| `cod_enterable` | boolean | whether gameplay can enter it |
| `cod_floors` | integer | authored floor count |

The empty's X/Y dimensions define its footprint and its Z extent defines the
height. Irregular future buildings may use a planar metadata mesh instead.

Trigger/interior boxes live under `WORLD/METADATA/VOLUMES` and use
`cod_role=volume`, a stable `cod_id`, and a `cod_kind`. `BOUND_playable` is a Cube
empty under `BOUNDS` and encloses the playable world.

Spatial facts belong in Blender. Non-spatial facts such as minimap labels,
gameplay categories, or script hooks belong in `world.meta.json`, keyed by the
same stable IDs so changes remain reviewable as text.

## Commands

Current migration commands:

```bash
npm run world                  # alias for the Blender world export
npm run world:export           # authoring export + runtime validation
npm run world:check            # fail if committed assets are stale
npm run world:validate         # DCC-independent runtime asset validation
npm run world:source:validate  # validate collections/properties in world.blend
npm run world:organize         # rebuild editable per-building region groups
```

Blender 5.2 LTS is required for authoring/export commands.

## Maintained export guarantees

Changes to the Blender source must continue to satisfy:

1. All screenshot baselines are within an explicitly accepted pixel tolerance.
2. Spawn, stairs, doors, roofs, perimeter, and surface-tag physics tests pass.
3. Approximately 220 world draw calls and 8,008 instances are retained.
4. Collision remains at approximately 38,580 triangles unless a reviewed edit
   intentionally changes it.
5. A clean checkout can run `npm run build` without Blender installed.
6. The runtime no longer imports authored layout data for queries; query regions
   come from the same manifest as the rendered and collision assets.
7. A pinned headless Blender export followed by `world:validate` is reproducible.

Python is encouraged for import, validation, metadata extraction, and deterministic
export orchestration. The `.blend` scene, not Python-generated geometry, becomes
the editable source after cutover.
